animation-worklet/idlharness.any.js*.description: the object of the test, `new WorkletAnimation("name")`, throws a TypeError: no animator named `name` is registered in the animation worklet ("If documentAnimatorDefinitions[animatorName] does not exists, throw an TypeError"), and the worker variant evaluates it in a worker, where `WorkletAnimation` (`[Exposed=Window]`) is not defined; `CSS.animationWorklet` is only exposed in the secure contexts, as the `Worklet` interface it returns, and the test is not served over HTTPS (see css/css-paint-api/idlharness.html); these subtests fail in every browser

animation-worklet/inactive-timeline.http.description: the test uses the `scrollSource` option and attribute of `ScrollTimeline`, of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source`; the times are now progress-based instead of the times of a `timeRange`): `animation.timeline.scrollSource` is undefined and the test throws; fails in every browser

animation-worklet/playback-rate.https.ht.description: the scroll-linked subtests use the `scrollSource` option and attribute of `ScrollTimeline`, of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source`): `animation.timeline.scrollSource` is undefined and they throw (the last one waits for a local time in milliseconds that a progress-based timeline never gives: it times out); they fail in every browser

`The playback rate set before the animation started playing...` expects the current time to progress from the timeline time of the `play()` call: the animation starts when its pending play task runs, at the next frame (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#playing-an-animation-section), so the current time is one frame (16.7 ms × the playback rate) behind; the Chromium implementation of the time of the test set the start time in `play()`

animation-worklet/scroll-timeline-writin.description: the test creates its timeline with `new ScrollTimeline({ scrollSource, orientation })`, the options of an old draft of Scroll-driven Animations (now `source` and `axis`, with progress-based times instead of the times of a `timeRange`): the unknown members are ignored, so the timeline is the scroll timeline of the scrolling element of the document, which does not scroll (its progress stays 0%, so the transform is the one of the first keyframe); fails in every browser

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-anim.description: the test has no encoding declaration and one of its animator names is Persian: decoded as windows-1252 (UTF-8 is not detected for a document of the network, as in the browsers: `encoding-detection/utf-8.html`), the name contains code points that are not identifier code points (U+00AF, U+00B2…), so `registerAnimator()` throws a TypeError ("If name is not a valid <ident>") and the module does not register the animators

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-crea.description: `new WorkletAnimation('test-animator', [])` is expected to throw a NotSupportedError: the draft creates a WorkletGroupEffect without children (https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-animation-worklet-1/#dom-workletanimation-workletanimation); `new WorkletAnimation('unregistered-animator', effect)` is expected to throw an InvalidStateError DOMException: the draft, which is followed, throws a TypeError ("If documentAnimatorDefinitions[animatorName] does not exists, throw an TypeError"); both are behaviors of the former Chromium implementation; they fail in every browser

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-loca.description: the last two subtests wait for `animation.currentTime > 1000` on an animation whose effect ends at 1000 ms: a worklet animation is an animation, which is finished and whose current time is limited to the end of its effect (https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#update-an-animations-finished-state), so the animator never gets a current time over 1000 and the subtest times out; the worklet animations of the former Chromium implementation never finished

animation-worklet/worklet-animation-with.description: `play()` is expected to throw an InvalidStateError for an effect without keyframes: neither Web Animations nor the Animation Worklet draft make such an effect invalid (a behavior of the former Chromium implementation); fails in every browser

css/css-animations/event-dispatch.tentat.description: the elapsed time of `animationcancel` is 0 when the timeline is set to null or `cancel()` is called, and seeking from the after phase to the before phase fires `animationend` instead of `animationstart`

css/css-backgrounds/animations/backgroun.description: the interpolation from `currentcolor` to a translucent color is off by one unit (`rgba(0, 209, 46, 0.69)` instead of `rgba(0, 208, 47, 0.69)`)
the `cross-fade()` values of the test are not supported

css/css-backgrounds/background-image-cor.description: the images of the computed styles are fetched by the rendering updates and do not delay the `load` event: the two fetches of the image (with and without CORS) have no resource timing entry yet when the `load` event handler reads the performance timeline

css/css-backgrounds/parsing/background-p.description: contradictory expectations, `x-start` alone computes to `x-start` but `0.5em, x-start, x-end` expects `20px, 0%, 100%` (fails in every browser)
contradictory expectations, `y-start` alone computes to `y-start` but `0.5em, y-start, y-end` expects `20px, 0%, 100%` (fails in every browser)

css/css-backgrounds/parsing/background-v.description: `background: none` expects `background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` while `background: border-box content-box` expects `transparent` for the same initial value (fails in every browser)

css/css-borders/corner-shape/corner-shap.description: `superellipse(-.8)`: the line next to the corner starts at 90.1px where the test expects 88px with a tolerance of 2px: the extent of the flattened contour in the band of the line is the exact one, the browsers sample the shape per pixel row

`notch` and `notch bevel` with `border-radius: 50%`: a horizontal edge of the contour lies on the boundary between the two middle line boxes (an arm of the zero-width cross that four notches leave, a side of the triangle that a notch and a bevel leave); an edge that only touches the block-start or the block-end of the band of a line is not in the band, so the line above the edge is not shortened (120px instead of 60px)

css/css-borders/outline-offset-rounding..description: `outline-offset` is not snapped to device pixels like `outline-width`

css/css-borders/tentative/parsing/border.description: the newer `border-clip` grammar (`normal`, unitless `0` kept); the webref grammar `none | [<length-percentage> | <flex>]+` is used
the newer `border-clip` grammar (`normal` instead of `none`); the webref grammar is used
the newer `border-clip` grammar (`normal`, unitless `0` kept); the webref grammar is used

css/css-borders/tentative/parsing/box-sh.description: expects the unitless `0` of a `<length>` to be kept in the specified value (it is serialized as `0px`, as the browsers do for the other length properties); no browser implements `box-shadow-blur`

expects the named colors of `red, blue` to be serialized as `rgb()` in the specified value, while `red` alone is kept (named colors are kept in the specified value); no browser implements `box-shadow-color`
expects the unitless `0` of `10px 0` and `0 10px` to be kept in the computed value, while `0 0` computes to `0px`; no browser implements `box-shadow-offset`
expects the unitless `0` of a `<length>` to be kept in the specified value (it is serialized as `0px`, as the browsers do for the other length properties); no browser implements `box-shadow-offset`
expects the unitless `0` of a `<length>` to be kept in the specified value (it is serialized as `0px`, as the browsers do for the other length properties); no browser implements `box-shadow-spread`

css/css-box/margin-trim/computed-margin-.description: the test expects the margins of the flex and grid items that `margin-trim` trimmed in an old draft to compute to `0`: the trimming of the items of the flex and grid containers was removed from the property (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13731: it applies to the block containers and the multi-column containers, and its `inline` values are no longer valid), and a trimmed margin keeps its resolved value (css/css-box/margin-trim/margin-trim-computed-value.html); as in Chrome

css/css-cascade/declaration-context.html.description: the at-rules nested in `@scope` (`@keyframes`, `@page`, `@position-try`) are not parsed as in a style sheet: their declarations are dropped, or the rule cannot be inserted with `insertRule()`

css/css-cascade/presentational-hints-rol.description: `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` of images and iframes (natural and default sizes) when `revert` rolls back the `width`/`height` hints

css/css-cascade/revert-val-006.html.description: `revert` in a keyframe is the underlying value instead of rolling back to the user-agent value

css/css-cascade/revert-val-007.html.description: `revert` in a keyframe is the underlying value instead of rolling back to the user-agent value

css/css-cascade/scope-implicit-construct.description: an implicit `@scope` (without prelude) in a constructed style sheet adopted by a document: the tests expect the document to be its scoping root (the scoped rules match the root element, and `:scope` matches no element)

css/css-cascade/scope-name-defining-rule.description: the `@keyframes` rules nested in `@scope` are ignored

css/css-color-hdr/parsing.html.description: expects `dynamic-range-limit-mix()` with a single parameter or with percentages that sum to zero to be invalid, but the spec now takes one or more parameters, like `color-mix()` (w3c/csswg-drafts#14454), and a zero sum computes to the initial value (w3c/csswg-drafts#11678)

css/css-color/light-dark-image.html.description: `-webkit-cross-fade()` in property values (the nested `image-set(-webkit-cross-fade(...))` does not parse)

css/css-color/parsing/color-computed-pow.description: a computed value with a negative lightness or a hue that serializes as 360 cannot round-trip, as parsing clamps the lightness and normalizes the hue (fails in every browser)

css/css-color/parsing/color-computed-rel.description: two subtests convert from and to `rec2020` with the pure 2.4 gamma transfer function of the current CSS Color 4 draft (ITU-R BT.1886), while the library, as every browser and the rec2020 reftests, uses the piecewise ITU-R BT.2020 transfer function (1.0993 * L^0.45 - 0.0993): `color(from color(rec2020 0.25 0.5 0.75) srgb r g b)` is `color(srgb -0.280036 0.565528 0.79951)` instead of `color(srgb -0.328686 0.491201 0.76185)`; fails in every browser

css/css-conditional/container-queries/co.description: `CSS.registerProperty()` accepts container query units (`cqw`...) in `initialValue`, although they are not computationally independent (it must throw SyntaxError)
`calc()` in an `SVGLength`, and setting the `value` of an `SVGLength` with a CSS unit (it keeps the unit instead of becoming a number)

css/css-conditional/container-queries/sc.description: the queries `(scrollable: var(...))` are not in a `scroll-state()` function: they are unknown features (`<general-enclosed>`), which never match (fails in Chrome too)
after the scroll of an arrow key, the `scroll-state(scrolled)` query of the container does not match the direction of the scroll (`--scrolled` is `no`)
the relative scroll (`scrollBy()`) made by the `scroll` listener of a user scroll ends at 158.56 instead of 150: the user scroll of the other container is still applied
after the scroll of `PageUp`, the `scroll-state(scrolled)` query of the container does not match the direction of the scroll (`PageDown` does)
the scroll of the space key changes the `scroll-state(scrolled)` state of the container where the test expects it unchanged
the first snap of a scroll container fires no `scrollsnapchange` event (the layout is computed lazily)

css/css-conditional/js/CSS-supports-deta.description: `::details-content` cannot be followed by `::before`, `::first-line` or `:lang()` in a selector (`CSS.supports("selector(...)")` is false)

css/css-conditional/match-container-chan.description: `matchContainer()` evaluates its queries in a `display: none` subtree: it fires `change` while hidden and does not skip a hidden ancestor container

css/css-contain/content-visibility/conte.description: `scrollWidth` is expected without the inline-end margin of the child, but the scrollable overflow includes it (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-3/#scrollable): all the browsers fail the test

the size containment is expected as soon as the element stops being relevant to the user (before the next rendering update, which determines its proximity to the viewport), and its last remembered size (`content-visibility: auto` implies `contain-intrinsic-size: auto`) is ignored: all the browsers fail these subtests

css/css-easing/linear-timing-functions-s.description: the specified value of `linear(calc(0/0), 1)` is expected in its computed form (`linear(0 0%, 1 100%)`) while the other specified values keep their authored form (`linear(0, 1)`): Chrome and Firefox fail the authored forms, Safari fails this one

css/css-flexbox/intrinsic-size/row-use-c.description: an item that cannot shrink and whose flex basis is `auto` contributes its min-content size to the min-content size of the container (its flex base size under a min-content constraint, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#algo-main-item, as WPT css/css-flexbox/intrinsic-size/row-001.html expects); the subtest `no overflow 2` expects its max-content size, from the use cases of a proposed Chrome algorithm ("liberal pass conditions"; Chrome fails 3 of the 6 subtests, Firefox and Safari all of them)

css/css-fonts/animations/font-palette-an.description: the last subtest runs `@keyframes animFrom { from { font-palette: --custom } }` with `animation-fill-mode: forwards` on an element whose `style` attribute sets `font-palette: --custom`, and expects `normal` at the end of the animation: the neutral `to` keyframe is the underlying value (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-animations-1/#keyframes), `--custom`, so the animated value is `--custom`, as in Firefox and Safari (only Chrome returns `normal`)

css/css-fonts/animations/font-palette-in.description: the two subtests that read the computed value directly (`An interpolation to inherit updates correctly on a parent style change.`, `Test additive animations`) expect `palette-mix(in oklab, normal, light)`, with the default color space: the computed value is `palette-mix(normal, light)`, as `css/css-fonts/parsing/palette-mix-computed.html` requires since the color interpolation method of `palette-mix()` is optional (`palette-mix(in oklab, light 30%, dark)` computes to `palette-mix(light 30%, dark 70%)`); the test was not updated with that change of the specification (the interpolated values of the other 112 subtests are compared with the computed value of the expectation, and pass)

css/css-fonts/animations/font-variation-.description: the extrapolated axis values are not clamped to the largest single-precision float

css/css-fonts/animations/font-weight-com.description: the sum of the added font weights is rounded

css/css-fonts/calc-in-font-variation-set.description: the specified-value subtest reads the inline `div.style`, but the value is set in a style sheet rule (it fails in every browser)

css/css-fonts/fallback-url-to-local.html.description: the width of the text shaped with the font is measured (fallback to a `local()` font while the remote one loads)

css/css-fonts/font-style-angle.html.description: the specified values are kept as their serialization, whose numbers have 6 decimals (`oblique 0.785398165rad` is `oblique 0.785398rad`), and the computed value is computed from it: `44.999991deg` instead of `45deg`

css/css-fonts/generic-family-keywords-00.description: the `-webkit-generic()` subtests fail in every browser: the function is not a valid `<family-name>`, so the declaration is invalid

css/css-fonts/parsing/font-variant-seria.description: `font-variant` serializes to the empty string after `font: menu` (system font) when a `font-variant-*` longhand is set

css/css-fonts/test_font_family_parsing.h.description: family names of several identifiers that contain a CSS-wide keyword or `default` (e.g. `simple default`, `inherit simple`) are rejected in `font-family` and `font`

css/css-fonts/test_font_feature_values_p.description: `@font-feature-values bongo { @blah } @styleset {...} }` is a syntax error for `insertRule()` (the `}` closes the rule), and the duplicate declarations of a feature value block are expected in the serialization although the block is a map (fails in every browser)

css/css-fonts/variations/at-font-face-de.description: the test contradicts itself: an `oblique` range with equal bounds is collapsed (`oblique 10deg 10deg` is `oblique 10deg`, as the `font-weight` and `font-width` ranges), but `oblique 20deg 20deg` (the former default angle) is expected as written; Chrome fails the first subtest, Safari the second

css/css-fonts/variations/at-font-face-fo.description: expects an oblique face with an angle of the opposite sign to be preferred over an italic face; https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts-4/#font-style-matching checks the italic faces before the oblique angles of the opposite sign

css/css-fonts/variations/font-stretch.ht.description: the test expects the huge computed percentage `1e9%` in exponent form (`1e+009%`); `1000000000%` is returned

css/css-forms/appearance-base-cursor.htm.description: the cursors of the controls (`default`, `text`, `not-allowed`, also for a `label` and an `input type=range` without base appearance; csswg-drafts#14251) are not in the Basic Appearance User Agent Stylesheet of the specification, which the library applies: the controls inherit `cursor: pointer` from the body (only Chrome passes)

css/css-forms/input-file-base-appearance.description: the test expects a `border-radius` of 0.5em for `::file-selector-button`; the style sheet of the specification gives the buttons and the button-like controls `border-radius: 4px`

css/css-forms/input-text-base-appearance.description: the test expects no `border-radius`, `align-items: normal` (initial) and `user-select: auto` for a text field with base appearance; the style sheet of the specification gives it `border-radius: 4px` and `align-items: unsafe center`

css/css-grid/alignment/self-baseline/gri.description: the non-standard `-webkit-text-orientation` alias of Blink and WebKit (the test passes with `text-orientation: sideways`)

css/css-grid/grid-definition/grid-inline.description: expects the resolved value `none` for the implicit tracks of a grid without explicit tracks; all the browsers return the sizes of the implicit tracks

css/css-grid/grid-definition/grid-templa.description: expects the resolved value `none` for the implicit tracks of a grid without explicit tracks; all the browsers return the sizes of the implicit tracks

css/css-grid/grid-lanes/intrinsic-sizing.description: the size containment of a `select` list box keeps the space of its scrollbar, as in the browsers (its contents are replaced by `contain-intrinsic-size`)

css/css-grid/parsing/grid-template-colum.description: the intrinsic auto repetitions (`repeat(auto-fill, auto)`, tentative; no browser implements them)

css/css-grid/parsing/grid-template-rows-.description: the intrinsic auto repetitions (`repeat(auto-fill, auto)`, tentative; no browser implements them)

css/css-images/idlharness.html.description: `CSS.elementSources` (the element sources of the `element()` function, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#elementsources); no browser implements it

css/css-inline/baseline-source/baseline-.description: the test depends on overlay scrollbars: in the two `vertical-rl` cases whose line of 100px overflows the inline axis of the `textarea`, the classic scrollbar displayed at its block-start edge shifts its first line by 15px (`offsetLeft` 10 instead of 25); Chrome fails the same way

css/css-inline/inheritance.html.description: the test checks the properties of an old draft of CSS Inline (`initial-letters`, `initial-letters-align`, `initial-letters-wrap`, `initial-sizing`)

css/css-link-params/*.description: CSS Linked Parameters (`link-parameters`, the `param()` modifier of `url()`): the property is parsed with the grammar of webref only, so the typed parameters (`param(--a type(<color>), orange)`) are rejected, the parameters without value (`param(--a)`) are accepted, the empty value is serialized as `param(--a,)` and `currentcolor` is computed; no browser implements the specification

css/css-logical/animations/logical-short.description: the logical shorthands of a keyframe are not prioritized by their number of longhands

css/css-masking/animations/clip-path-int.description: the interpolation of `shape()` with a `path()` (the path is not converted to the equivalent `shape()`, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-shapes-2/#interpolating-shape: the values are not interpolated) and of the `arc` commands whose `cw`/`ccw` or `large`/`small` options differ

css/css-masking/parsing/mask-valid.sub.h.description: the expected longhands of `mask` do not include `mask-border-mode`, which the shorthand resets with the other `mask-border-*` longhands (https://drafts.fxtf.org/css-masking/#the-mask: "also resets mask-border", whose longhands include `mask-border-mode`; WPT css/css-masking/mask-shorthand-subproperties-reset.html expects it reset); the browsers do not support `mask-border-mode`

css/css-mixins/function-property-context.description: the `em` units of the arguments, defaults, locals and result of a custom function do not resolve in the calling context of the property (32px instead of 20px)

css/css-mixins/functions/function-shadow.description: the custom functions defined in a shadow tree are not resolved in the keyframes

css/css-mixins/private/private-cssom-ser.description: the serialization of `@private` keeps the repeated declarations of a variable (`--x: 1px; --x: 2px;` instead of the last one)

css/css-multicol/multicol-fill-balance-0.description: the test relies on the saturation of the layout units of Blink: the content of the nested multi-column container is 1,234,567,990px tall, more than the largest length of Blink (2^25 px), and is expected to fit in the two outer columns of 20,000,000px; the outer container gets 62 columns (the lengths are not limited)

css/css-multicol/scroll-width-height.ten.description: `scrollWidth`/`scrollHeight` of a fragmented box (the scrollable overflow of its fragments stitched together); the first fragment is used

css/css-overflow/parsing/line-clamp-vali.description: `line-clamp: 3 ellipsis auto` (with or without `-webkit-legacy`) is valid with the grammar of https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13670 (`[ <integer [1,∞]> || auto || <'block-ellipsis'> ] -webkit-legacy?`), but the test expects it to serialize as specified: the shorthand serializes its longhands in the canonical order of the grammar and omits the default `ellipsis` (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-value), as the same test expects for `8 ellipsis` (serialized as `8`) and `auto 11` (serialized as `11 auto`), so the value is `3 auto`

css/css-overflow/resizer-transform.tenta.description: the `resize` property (resizing the box by dragging its resizer)

css/css-overflow/scroll-markers/scroll-m.description: expects a clicked `::scroll-marker` to match `:focus` in the default (links) mode of `scroll-marker-group`, which contradicts the specification ("If the scroll marker group is in links mode: set the sequential focus navigation starting point to the originating element, losing focus from the scroll marker") and `scroll-marker-activation-retains-focus.html`; the rest of the test (the next Tab focuses the scroll target) works

css/css-paint-api/idlharness.html.description: the test is not served over HTTPS: `CSS.paintWorklet` is only exposed in the secure contexts, as the `Worklet` interface it returns (as in Chromium; the IDL of the specification does not annotate the attribute, although the worklets only exist in the secure contexts); the subtest fails in every browser

css/css-overflow/scrollable-overflow-pad.description: a `vertical-rl` container (labeled `VLR + RTL`) expects a box moved leftwards, into the reachable scrollable overflow, not to contribute to it

css/css-overflow/scrollable-overflow-tra.description: tentative test of the open issue https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/12113: the untransformed border box of an in-flow child extends the in-flow content of its scroll container (and so its scrolling area, with the paddings), as in Chrome and Firefox, which fail the same 2 subtests with the same values; the test expects it to be excluded
the tentative unreachable region of the transformed boxes (their transformed bounds are clipped at the scroll origin)

css/css-page/page-rule-declarations-004..description: a dashed ident (`--a`) is accepted as an `@page` selector, as in Chrome, Firefox and Safari: it is an `<ident-token>`, which the grammar of the page selectors (`<page-selector> = [ <ident-token>? <pseudo-page>* ]!`) accepts

css/css-page/parsing/margin-rules-002.ht.description: the last three subtests read `pagerule.style.paddingLeft`: `CSSPageRule.style` is a `CSSPageDescriptors` (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#csspagedescriptors), a `CSSStyleDeclaration` whose only attributes are the page descriptors (`margin*`, `size`, `pageOrientation`, `marks`, `bleed`), so `paddingLeft` is undefined (the declaration is kept: `getPropertyValue("padding-left")` returns `10px`); Blink exposes every property there, Gecko fails these subtests

css/css-page/parsing/page-orientation-co.description: the test expects `getComputedStyle(elm).pageOrientation` to be the empty string, but `page-orientation` is only a descriptor of `@page` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-page-3/#page-orientation-prop), and a `CSSStyleProperties` only has the camel-cased attributes of the supported CSS properties (https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-cssstyleproperties-camel_cased_attribute): the attribute is undefined, as in Gecko (Blink implements the descriptor as an internal property)

css/css-position/backdrop-tree-abiding-s.description: `::backdrop` after `::slotted()` (the tree-abiding pseudo-elements of the slotted elements)

css/css-position/position-absolute-perce.description: the image of a `data:` URL is not available synchronously: the layout checked by the script that follows the image has no natural size yet (the browsers decode it before)

css/css-position/sticky/position-sticky-.description: `getClientRects()` of a sticky inline box split around a sticky block-level box returns the border box of the block at its own sticky position (60px) for the part of the inline box that contains it, instead of that part shifted by the sticky offset of the inline box only (50px); a block-level box that is not sticky itself does not follow the sticky offset of the inline box it is split out of (Firefox fails it too)
the sticky positioning against the scroll containers of a single axis (`@supports named-feature()` of the proposal)

the iteration composite operation of the `<length-percentage>` lists of the registered custom properties accumulates the final value too many times
an additive `<transform-function>#` animation is not updated when the length of the underlying list changes (`scale(6)` instead of `scale(5)`)

additive `<transform-list>` animations: the underlying value is not updated from `none`, and an animation stacked on a discrete `var(--invalid, invalid)` animation is added to the base value instead of replacing it
`transition-property: all` does not include the registered custom properties
the interpolation of the `<transform-function>` and `<transform-list>` registered custom properties with a matrix fallback (`mix()`)
the interpolation of the `<transform-function>` and `<transform-list>` registered custom properties with a matrix fallback (`mix()`)
the interpolation of the `<transform-function>` and `<transform-list>` registered custom properties with a matrix fallback (`mix()`)

css/css-properties-values-api/at-propert.description: a change of the initial value of a `@property` rule does not start a transition

css/css-properties-values-api/font-prope.description: font-relative units in `calc()` in the font properties resolve against the element's own font instead of the parent's (csswg-drafts#8169), and registered `<length>` values give 0 in `font-size`

the `<integer>` registered custom properties with `ex` and `cap` are rounded but compared with the unrounded length (0.1 tolerance): they pass only when the x-height and the cap height of the default font are whole numbers of px

css/css-properties-values-api/register-p.description: the test expects `CSS.registerProperty()` to throw a TypeError without the `inherits` member, which has a default value in the IDL of the specification (`boolean inherits = true`, https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-properties-values-api-1/#dictdef-propertydefinition); the browsers still require it

css/css-properties-values-api/resolved-c.description: `sibling-index()` in the channels of `color()` is rejected for a registered `<color>` property (falls back to the initial value)

css/css-properties-values-api/var-refere.description: `var()` referencing a registered `<length>` property declared with an invalid value (`red`) substitutes `0px` instead of making the referencing property invalid

css/css-pseudo/CSSPseudoElement-getBoxQu.description: the margin box of the block-level `::before` includes its used margin-right (the over-constrained margin of CSS 2 §10.3.3, 147px in a 200px container); the test (Blink) expects its computed margin (3px)

css/css-pseudo/events-on-after-before-ma.description: the sub-pseudo-element `::after::marker`: the box of the marker of a `::before`/`::after` list item is a box of its pseudo-element (it has no box quads and is hit as the `::after`)

css/css-pseudo/events-on-pseudo-element-.description: the sub-pseudo-elements `::before::marker` and `::after::marker`: their boxes are hit as the `::before`/`::after` (the `pseudoTarget` of `::before` and its retargeting pass)

css/css-pseudo/events-on-pseudo-element..description: the CSS animations and transitions of `::scroll-marker`: the test times out waiting for the `animationstart` event of its animation (the `pseudoTarget` of the animation, transition and focus events is not defined, UI Events only adds it to `UIEvent`)

css/css-pseudo/idlharness.html.description: the setup calls `window.getPseudoElements()` and uses `CSSPseudoElementList`, which were removed from CSS Pseudo-Elements 4 (they are not in its IDL): the tests of the `CSSPseudoElement` object fail

css/css-pseudo/input-element-pseudo-open.description: the pickers of the date/time/color/datalist inputs (clicking does not open a picker, so `:open` never matches)
`HTMLInputElement.showPicker()` always throws `NotAllowedError` (no picker UI), so `:open` never matches

css/css-pseudo/parsing/marker-supported-.description: expects the computed `list-style` to include `outside` (it contradicts css/css-lists/parsing/list-style-computed.sub.html)
the computed `list-style` shorthand of `::marker` is serialized as `outside` instead of `outside none disc`

html/browsers/the-window-object/named-ac.description: as in the browsers, a cross-origin caller gets the child navigable named `frame1` from the WindowProxy of its parent (`window.parent.frame1`) even when the document of that child is cross-origin with the parent; the HTML Standard only exposes the names of the document-tree child navigable target name property set (the children that are same origin with the window) and throws a SecurityError for the others. Other web-platform-tests rely on the behavior of the browsers (`web-animations/timing-model/timelines/sibling-iframe-timeline.html`, `document_domain_access_details.sub.html`). 2 subtests of 3: Firefox and Safari fail them too, Chrome fails the first one

html/browsers/the-window-object/open-clo.description: `callback = t.step(function() { assert_unreached() })` calls the function immediately instead of storing it (fails in every browser)

`test_driver.create_window()` and `test_driver.navigate()` with a window handle are not implemented by the runner: there is no top-level browsing context created by WebDriver (not by web content) to check that it is not script-closable (1 subtest of 2)

html/browsers/the-window-object/security.description: `window.onmousewheel`, a non-standard event handler attribute of Blink and WebKit that no specification defines (1 subtest of 124; Firefox fails it too)

html/browsers/the-window-object/window-o.description: the test expects `noopener` and `noreferrer` to always open a tab, as Chrome and Safari do; the HTML Standard removes `noopener` and `noreferrer` from the tokenized features, then checks if a popup window is requested with the remaining ones (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window-open-steps), so e.g. `resizable=yes,scrollbars=yes,status=yes,noopener` is a popup (26 subtests of 51; Firefox fails the same ones)

html/browsers/the-window-object/window-r.description: the test is outdated, as it says (https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3267#issuecomment-2788132131): it expects the `load` event of an iframe without `src` (or with `src=""` or `about:blank`) not to be fired while the iframe is inserted (6 subtests of 7; fails in every browser)

`window.open("about:blank", name)` keeps the initial `about:blank` document of the new popup (the window open steps only run the URL and history update steps for an `about:blank` URL), so the first navigation away from it reuses its Window object as specified; the tentative test expects the Window not to be reused, as in the browsers (1 subtest of 2)

html/browsers/windows/clear-window-name..description: the document.domain case sets `document.domain` to a host with a port, which throws (it also times out in Chrome and Safari)

html/browsers/windows/consume-user-activ.description: `window.open()` does not consume the user activation of the entry global object (with multiple globals involved)

html/browsers/windows/nested-browsing-co.description: expects `frames["iframe_2"]` to return a cross-origin child navigable named by its iframe `name` attribute, as the browsers do; the target name of a cross-origin navigable is not in the document-tree child navigable target name property set of the window, so the named property is undefined

resource-timing/render-blocking-status-s.description: a Chrome-only test (Firefox and Safari do not implement `renderBlockingStatus`) of the behavior of Chrome: `renderBlockingStatus` is `blocking` for the scripts that are render-blocking when they are prepared, but the test also expects `blocking` for a `blocking=render` script inserted into the head by a script of the body (`script-head-blocking-render-dynamic-dom`): the body element exists, so the document does not allow adding render-blocking elements and, per the specification, the script is not render-blocking (the render-blocking of its request is only set when it is "currently render-blocking")

selection/fire-selectionchange-event-on-.description: `execCommand("delete")` in a focused `<input>` of a shadow tree deletes the character and fires `selectionchange` at the input, as the Selection API specifies for a text control (the event bubbles and is composed to the document, retargeted to the shadow host). shadow-dom/focus/click-focus-slot-ancest.description: 1 of 3 subtests: a drag that selects the text slotted in a non-focusable `<slot>` of a shadow tree whose content is editable (`contenteditable` on the shadow host's parent), inside a focusable `<div tabindex=0>` of the shadow tree, focuses that `<div>` (`shadowRoot.activeElement` is the `<div id=shadowDiv>`); the test expects the focus to be on the editing host only (`shadowRoot.activeElement` null), as Chrome and Safari do: the press focuses the first click-focusable flat-tree ancestor of the target, which is the `<div>` before the editing host (Firefox fails this subtest too).

shadow-dom/imperative-slot-api-cross-sha.description: the test expects a `slotchange` at a slot whose assigned nodes do not change: `slotB.assign(nodeN)` with a node that is not a child of the host of `slotB` ("slotB slotchange should fire because it gained its assigned node (even if not rendered)"); the DOM Standard only signals a slot change when the assigned nodes of the slot change (https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#assign-slotables), as Safari does (wpt.fyi: Safari fails this subtest with the same assertion, "expected 1 but got 0"; Chrome and Firefox fire the event). shadow-dom/wheel-event-related-target.ht.description: the test expects `relatedTarget` of the `wheel` events to be the element under the pointer (retargeted to the shadow host); UI Events defines no related target for the wheel events, and the attribute is null in every browser (wpt.fyi: Chrome, Firefox and Safari fail with the same "relatedTarget before mouse is over shadow host expected Element node <div id=\"container\"> but got null")

the coverage of the antialiased edges is the exact area of the pixels, which differs slightly from the one of the browsers the fuzziness of the test is tuned for: 166 pixels of the edges of the shape differ (by up to 2), 16 are allowed

the outline of a `superellipse(-0.5)` corner: the curve of the contour is the quarter of an ellipse between the tangents of its two ends for the parameters between -1 and 0 (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#border-aligned-corner-clip-out-path), and the reference draws Bézier curves of the superellipse, which start in another direction: the edges differ by up to 73/255 on 175 pixels (the test allows 46/255; it fails in all the browsers)

the coverage of the antialiased edges is the exact area of the pixels, which differs slightly from the one of the browsers the fuzziness of the test is tuned for: 370 pixels of the concave corners differ (by up to 70), 347 are allowed

css/css-borders/corner-shape/render-corn.description: 3 of the variants differ from the reference: a 100% `border-top-left-radius` with `corner-shape: 1` and a 20px border, and a 100% `border-top-right-radius` with an inset shadow (with `corner-shape: 1` and 20px top and bottom borders, or without `corner-shape`)

css/css-borders/tentative/border-radius-.description: the test reads `border-top-radius: 1em 4em / 2em 3em` as the two radii of each corner (`1em 4em` for the first corner), where the values before the slash are the horizontal radii of the two corners and the values after it their vertical radii, as in `border-radius` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#corner-sizing-side-shorthands); the green borders painted over the red ones of the same shape also leave red antialiased edges, and the test has no fuzzy tolerance (see its TODO)

the test reads `border-top-radius: 1em 4em / 2em 3em` as the two radii of each corner (`1em 4em` for the first corner), where the values before the slash are the horizontal radii of the two corners and the values after it their vertical radii, as in `border-radius` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-borders-4/#corner-sizing-side-shorthands); the green borders painted over the red ones of the same shape also leave red antialiased edges, and the test has no fuzzy tolerance (see its TODO)

css/css-box/margin-trim/flex-*.description: the test checks the trimming of the margins of the flex items, which was removed from `margin-trim` (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13731): the property applies to the block containers and the multi-column containers only, and its `inline` values are no longer valid (css/css-box/parsing/margin-trim.html); as in Chrome

css/css-box/margin-trim/grid-*.description: the test checks the trimming of the margins of the grid items, which was removed from `margin-trim` (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13731): the property applies to the block containers and the multi-column containers only, and its `inline` values are no longer valid (css/css-box/parsing/margin-trim.html); as in Chrome

css/css-break/flexbox/flex-container-fra.description: an empty flex container with `contenteditable`, a block-start padding of 20px and a block-end padding of 100px, in columns of 50px: the container has no line box (it is 120px tall) and is not broken (an empty box has no possible break between its paddings: it overflows the first column), where Blink gives the empty editable container the block size of a line (`line-height: 80px`), which is monolithic and overflows the first column, and places the block-end padding in the second one (a 100px by 100px square)

css/css-break/flexbox/multi-line-row-fle.description: the gap between two lines of a row flex container (`row-gap: 100px`) at a forced break: the gap disappears and the next line starts the next column, where the reference keeps 50px before the line in each of the next columns (as a `margin-top: 50px` that is preserved after a forced break); the rule that Blink applies could not be determined from this test alone (the part of the gap that does not fit in the previous column is 50px after the first column, but 100px after the next ones), so the gap is still suppressed as at an unforced break

css/css-break/out-of-flow-in-multicolumn.description: an absolutely positioned box in a relatively positioned block split out of an inline box with a filter (the containing block of the fixed positioned box that the absolutely positioned box contains): the fragments of the absolutely positioned box in the 13th and 14th columns have no block size and its 200px child is not sliced between them, and the fixed positioned box, at its static position after that child, starts one column early (in the 14th column instead of the 15th)

the scrollable overflow of the viewport includes the 10000px tall absolutely positioned box whose containing block has `overflow-y: clip`: the box is laid out from the empty fragment of its containing block at the end of the first column, and its overflow is not clipped there. The viewport gets a vertical scrollbar that the reference does not have (the green square is the expected one); only Chrome passes (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

css/css-break/overflow-clip-010.html.description: a multi-column container nested in a box with `overflow: clip` that is fragmented is monolithic: its columns are not placed in the outer columns (only the in-flow nested containers that no ancestor clips are)

css/css-break/transform-009.html.description: an absolutely positioned box placed before the block-start edge of its transformed containing block, in the columns before it: its fragments there are children of empty fragments of the containing block (at the end of these columns), whose transform is not the one the reference expects (no browser passes this test)

css/css-break/flexbox/multi-line-row-fle.description: a multi-line row flex container in a nested multi-column container that is broken by the outer columns (analyzed on multi-line-row-flex-fragmentation-039; -059 has the same structure, with a margin before the item): the inner column where the line with an item with `break-inside: avoid` starts is moved to the next outer column with the whole line (a row of inner columns ends before a column whose break violates a rule), so the first row has 4 inner columns instead of 5, and the line then ends 50px later for the item that can be broken than for the other one (two stripes of 5px by 50px are not covered); Blink starts the line in the fifth inner column of the first row with the item that can be broken and pushes the item with `break-inside: avoid` alone to the next column: here an item at the start of its line is not pushed without its line

five lines without block size (each item has `margin-top: -100px; height: 100px`) with a forced break before each item: the lines without block size that are at the start of a column are all placed in it (the forced breaks between two tracks at the same position are not taken one after the other), so the five items are in the first column, where Blink places one item per column, 100px before the block-start edge of the column (the margin after a forced break is preserved)

a multi-line row flex container in a nested multi-column container that is broken by the outer columns (analyzed on multi-line-row-flex-fragmentation-039; -059 has the same structure, with a margin before the item): the inner column where the line with an item with `break-inside: avoid` starts is moved to the next outer column with the whole line (a row of inner columns ends before a column whose break violates a rule), so the first row has 4 inner columns instead of 5, and the line then ends 50px later for the item that can be broken than for the other one (two stripes of 5px by 50px are not covered); Blink starts the line in the fifth inner column of the first row with the item that can be broken and pushes the item with `break-inside: avoid` alone to the next column: here an item at the start of its line is not pushed without its line

css/css-break/flexbox/single-line-row-fl.description: a monolithic item with `margin-top: 5px` beside a taller monolithic item, in a multi-column container without block size (its columns are 1px tall): the item starts after the end of the first column and is placed when the flow of the container reaches its offset, in the sixth column, where Blink pushes it to the second column and keeps its 5px offset there; pushing an item that starts after the end of a column to the start of the next one was tried and breaks single-line-row-flex-fragmentation-043 (an item aligned to the end of a tall container keeps its offset in the container)

css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/grid-lanes.description: an empty grid lanes container with `contenteditable`, a block-start padding of 20px and a block-end padding of 100px, in columns of 50px: the container has no line box (it is 120px tall) and is not broken (an empty box has no possible break between its paddings: it overflows the first column), where Blink gives the empty editable container the block size of a line (`line-height: 80px`), which is monolithic and overflows the first column, and places the block-end padding in the second one (a 100px by 100px square); the same as css/css-break/flexbox/flex-container-fragmentation-007.tentative.html

the items are placed again in each column as in Gecko (the only browser that passes), except for the auto-placement cursor of the placement algorithm (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-layout-algorithm: "Choose the first line in possible lines greater than or equal to the auto-placement cursor"), which the reference, written before the cursor was specified, does not have: with `flow-tolerance: 0`, Gecko places an item whose tracks tie in the first one, the library in the first one after the tracks of the previous item (e.g. the 4th variant, columns of 48px: the 3rd pushed item, after an item placed in the 2nd track, goes to the 3rd track instead of the 2nd one); without the cursor, the library matches the 10 variants

the items (some of them span two tracks) are placed again in each column as in Gecko (the only browser that passes), except for the auto-placement cursor of the placement algorithm (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#grid-lanes-layout-algorithm), which the reference, written before the cursor was specified, does not have (with `flow-tolerance: 0px`, Gecko places an item whose tracks tie in the first ones); without the cursor, the library matches the 2 variants

css/css-break/grid/grid-lanes/row-grid-l.description: the item of the second row of the row grid lanes container (stacked in the inline axis) has no width: it is 0px wide (its max-content size) in every browser, so the red background is visible where the test expects it (it fails in every browser)

the fragmentation of a grid lanes container in its grid axis as the one of a grid (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#fragmentation): its rows are not tracks of parallel flows, the items are fragmented as block content; the forced break before the item of the second row (the first in-flow content of the container) is not taken, the row starts in the first column

css/css-break/table/caption-margin-005.h.description: a table caption with `margin-top: 200px` that follows a caption without block size, in a box that starts 50px before the end of the first column: the break between the two captions is a class A break that violates no rule, so the column ends in the margin and the box around the table has a fragment of 50px in the first column (its red background); in Blink the caption without block size gives no separation, so the break is taken before the box, and the margin, which then adjoins the break, is truncated in the second column

css/css-break/table/monolithic-overflow-.description: a cell with a monolithic child of 130px that overflows the first column (100px), followed by a child of 100px, beside a cell whose child has `height: 100%`, in a table of 200px: the row is 230px tall in the strip (the overflow of the monolithic child takes block size in its cell), so the child of the other cell is 230px tall and has 30px in a third column; in Blink the monolithic overflow takes no block size in the next column (the cell is 200px tall once fragmented, as the table): that needs the row to be laid out again with the block size of its fragmented cells

css/css-break/table/table-collapsed-bord.description: a break between two rows of a table with collapsed borders whose cells have different border widths (10px and 15px on a side): the collapsed borders of each fragment are painted from the fragments of its cells and clipped by the fragment, but the border of the row at the break and the corners where the borders of different widths meet at the break are not the ones of Blink (a few rows of pixels differ at the end of the second column and at the start of the third one)

css/css-color/color-mix-non-srgb-001.htm.description: the references are the colors of the test clipped to sRGB per channel, as the browsers paint them, while the library CSS gamut maps the colors outside of sRGB (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#css-gamut-mapping: the OkLCh chroma is reduced at constant lightness and hue): `color-mix(in lab, red, green)` is painted (160,108,0) instead of the clipped (161,108,0)

css/css-color/currentcolor-003.html.description: the `currentcolor` of `filter: drop-shadow()` on an inline box whose first fragment is on a first line with a `::first-line` color: the filter applies to the box as a whole (all its fragments) with the color of the style of the box, where the shadow of the fragment of the first line is expected in the `::first-line` color (the backgrounds, borders, outlines and shadows of the fragments are painted in it; only Firefox passes this test)

css/css-color/at-color-profile-001.html.description: the `@color-profile` rule and the custom color spaces (`color(--foo 0.6 0 0)` is parsed and kept in the computed value but is not converted with the ICC profile: the background is not painted); fails in every browser

css/css-color/clip-opacity-out-of-flow.h.description: the overflow clip of an ancestor of a stacking context (`overflow: hidden` 200x200 around the `opacity: 0.5` box) is applied to the whole group, including its absolutely and fixed positioned descendants whose containing block is outside of that clip: the blue and green boxes are clipped at 200px instead of at the 250px of the outer clip (10000 pixels)

css/css-color/color-layers-no-blend-mode.description: the resolution of `color-layers()` (css-color-6): the function is parsed and kept as is in the computed value, and the painter does not paint it (the backgrounds are transparent); fails in every browser

css/css-color/xyz-d50-004.html.description: the reference is `color(xyz-d50 0 1 0)` converted to sRGB with 6 digits (`color(srgb -1.20716 1.3163 -0.489014)`), the same color only when both are clipped per channel as in the browsers: the library CSS gamut maps them (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#css-gamut-mapping), and the rounding of the reference moves the mapped color by one level (152,255,198 instead of 152,255,199)

css/css-conditional/at-supports-namespac.description: the namespace prefix of `attr()` is not checked against the `@namespace` rules in `@supports` (`(content: attr(y|href))` is supported although `y` is not declared); fails in every browser

css/css-conditional/at-supports-selector.description: the `::-webkit-slider-thumb` pseudo-element: `@supports selector(input::-webkit-slider-thumb)` is false (the unknown `-webkit-` pseudo-elements are parsed, as the Compatibility Standard requires, but they are not supported)

css/css-conditional/container-queries/qu.description: a registered `<color>` custom property with a `none` component (`hwb(none 0 100)`, `color(srgb none 0 0)`, `oklch(0 0 none)`) is compared by `style(--c: black)` after its conversion to sRGB, where `none` is 0: the query matches although the computed values differ; only Firefox passes

css/css-conditional/container-queries/sc.description: the `cqw`/`cqh` units of a size container with `overflow: auto` are resolved against its content box minus the scrollbar that its contents trigger (85px); Chrome and Safari resolve them as if the automatic scrollbar was absent (100px, only `overflow: scroll` reserves the scrollbar)

css/css-contain/contain-layout-select-00.description: a `select` with layout containment (which has no baseline) is expected to be aligned as a `button` with layout containment, by the block-end edge of its content box (the test is tentative; Firefox passes it, Chrome and Safari do not): it is aligned by the block-end edge of its margin box, as the other atomic inlines without baseline

css/css-contain/contain-size-multicol-00.description: the child (50px tall) of a size-contained multi-column container without block size (`contain: size; column-count: 3`: columns of 0px) is cut in slices of 1px in overflow columns, which extend the scrollable overflow of the viewport horizontally (a horizontal scrollbar that the reference does not have); the browsers leave the child in the first column, which it overflows (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

the child (50px tall) of a size-contained multi-column container without block size (`contain: size; column-count: 3`: columns of 0px) is cut in slices of 1px in overflow columns, which extend the scrollable overflow of the viewport horizontally (a horizontal scrollbar that the reference does not have); the browsers leave the child in the first column, which it overflows (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

css/css-content/element-replacement-on-r.description: `content: url()` replaces the image of an `img` element (the yellow image is painted) but not the poster frame of a `video` element (the reference, which stays blue): the tentative test expects the replaced elements to behave the same; only Chrome passes (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/2831)

css/css-content/pseudo-element-image-set.description: an `image-set()` of a gradient in the `content` of a pseudo-element is not painted

css/css-content/quotes-030.html.description: the quotation marks of `quotes: auto` are the ones of the content language of the `q` element itself (as Chrome and Safari); the test expects the marks of the language of its parent (the language of the text around the quotation), as Firefox does (css-content: "based on the content language of the element and/or its parent")

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-clear-*.description: the test expects `clear` on a run-in box to apply to the block box it runs in to (CSS 2: "for run-in boxes, this property applies to the final block box to which the run-in box belongs"); CSS Display 3 formats the run-in box "as if originally parented there" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#run-in-layout), as an inline box, to which `clear` does not apply: the block stays beside the float

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-basic-007..description: the test expects a run-in box to run in to a block box with `overflow: scroll`; in CSS Display 3 a run-in sequence only runs in to "a block box that does not establish a new formatting context" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#run-in-layout): the header stays in an anonymous block before the scroll container

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-basic-006..description: the reference has no list marker: the run-in box runs in to the list item (after its marker), but the outside marker of the list item is painted in the margin of the body, where the reference has nothing

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-listitem-b.description: the test expects a run-in box followed by a list item not to run in (old CSS 2.1 drafts) and its reference has no list marker; in CSS Display 3 a list item is a block box: the run-in box runs in to the empty list item, after its marker (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display-3/#run-in-layout), and the outside markers of the two list items are painted in the margin of the body

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-float-betw.description: the run-in box runs in as expected, but the hidden right float ("Some text.") between the run-in box and the block shortens the first line of the block, which wraps earlier than in the reference, which has no float

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-replaced-0.description: the image runs in to the block and is sized as expected (100px square), but the text of the reference ("The blue square should be...") is not the text of the test ("Start of block. The blue square should be..."): the test cannot match

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-contains-i.description: the run-in box runs in as expected, but the reference expects the text of the float (in a table cell in an inline box of the run-in box) on the baseline of the line: the cell is wrapped in an anonymous inline-table whose row has no in-flow content, so its baseline is the bottom of the cell and the float is above the baseline of the line (as a float in a `display: table-cell` box of an inline box in Chrome)

css/css-display/run-in/run-in-contains-t.description: the run-in box runs in as expected, but the reference expects the text of the `display: table-caption` child on the baseline of the line: the caption is wrapped in an anonymous inline-table without row, whose baseline is its bottom margin edge, so the caption is above the baseline of the line (as a `display: table-caption` box in an inline box in Chrome)

css/css-flexbox/abspos/flex-abspos-align.description: an absolutely positioned child with `align-self: safe center` whose containing block is not the flex container, in a flex container whose writing mode is orthogonal to the one of the containing block: the overflowing box is aligned with the start edge of the inset-modified containing block in the cross axis of the flex container (it overflows the inset-modified containing block in that axis); the test expects the box centered there, as if the overflow were checked in the other axis of the containing block (where it fits), which is the behavior of Blink, the only browser that passes this tentative test of an open issue (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/11934, Blink aligns in the inset-modified containing block, Gecko in the static-position rectangle). The cases where the writing modes are parallel are rendered as expected

an absolutely positioned child with `align-self: safe center` whose containing block is not the flex container, in a flex container whose writing mode is orthogonal to the one of the containing block: the overflowing box is aligned with the start edge of the inset-modified containing block in the cross axis of the flex container (it overflows the inset-modified containing block in that axis); the test expects the box centered there, as if the overflow were checked in the other axis of the containing block (where it fits), which is the behavior of Blink, the only browser that passes this tentative test of an open issue (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/11934, Blink aligns in the inset-modified containing block, Gecko in the static-position rectangle). The cases where the writing modes are parallel are rendered as expected

css/css-flexbox/align-self-016.html.description: an item with `align-self: start` in a column wrap container keeps the cross size of its fit-content size in the inner cross size of the container (its hypothetical cross size, https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#algo-cross-item) when its line is wider than the container (another item is 200px wide in a 100px container); the test expects the item to be fitted again in the cross size of its line (only Chrome passes it)

css/css-flexbox/flex-container-line-if-e.description: an editable flex container without item "has a line if empty": it does not reserve the block size of one line (only Chrome passes this test)

css/css-flexbox/flex-container-max-conte.description: a matrix of the intrinsic sizes of the containers of one item (flexible, no-grow, no-shrink; with a preferred size smaller or larger than its contents; with a flex basis smaller or larger than them) that no browser passes: the row containers are rendered as expected but for 3 to 5 cases of an item that cannot grow or shrink whose flex basis and preferred size disagree (the reference sizes the container with the flex base size where the contribution of https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#intrinsic-item-contributions is larger); the block size of the column containers is the sum of the hypothetical main sizes of the items, where the reference expects the contributions of the items in the block axis too

css/css-flexbox/flex-container-min-conte.description: a matrix of the intrinsic sizes of the containers of one item (flexible, no-grow, no-shrink; with a preferred size smaller or larger than its contents; with a flex basis smaller or larger than them) that no browser passes: the row containers are rendered as expected but for 3 to 5 cases of an item that cannot grow or shrink whose flex basis and preferred size disagree (the reference sizes the container with the flex base size where the contribution of https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox-1/#intrinsic-item-contributions is larger); the block size of the column containers is the sum of the hypothetical main sizes of the items, where the reference expects the contributions of the items in the block axis too

css/css-flexbox/flexbox-basic-textarea-v.description: the text controls inherit their font (the HTML Standard gives them none; the browsers use a monospace font of 13.33px for a `textarea`): the `textarea` elements of the test inherit `8px monospace` from their flex container, the ones of the reference the 16px font of the body, whose line overflows their height of 10px and displays a vertical scrollbar (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

css/css-flexbox/intrinsic-size/col-wrap-.description: the max-content inline size of a multi-line column container whose block size is indefinite and whose maximum block size is a percentage (`max-height: 100%` of a definite height): the lines are broken at the maximum block size for the intrinsic size only when it is a length, so the container is as wide as one line (only Chrome passes this test)

css/css-flexbox/svg-no-natural-size-gran.description: the max-content contribution of a replaced element that only has an aspect ratio (an `svg` with a `viewBox`, `width="100%"` and `height="100%"`) is zero (as WPT css/css-sizing/svg-intrinsic-size-009.html expects for an `auto` width): the flex item that contains it has a flex base size of zero and stays empty, where the browsers give the element a non-zero contribution when its width is a percentage

css/css-font-loading/fontface-size-adjus.description: the `sizeAdjust` member of `FontFaceDescriptors` and the `FontFace.sizeAdjust` attribute (css-fonts-5): the glyphs of the `Ahem-large` face created by the script are not scaled by 200%

css/css-fonts/font-variant-emoji-005.htm.description: an emoji font (the keycap sequences in color): the bundled fonts have no color emoji

css/css-fonts/font-variant-emoji-1.html.description: an emoji font (U+263A with the text and emoji presentation selectors): the bundled fonts have no color emoji, so the two presentations use the same glyph

css/css-fonts/font-variant-position.html.description: expects the `subs`/`sups` glyphs of the test font for runs that contain characters the font has no subscript or superscript for: css-fonts-4 requires the synthesis of the whole run then ("simulated glyphs should be synthesized for all characters"; fails in Firefox, which synthesizes them, passes in Chrome, which does not)

css/css-fonts/matching/fixed-stretch-sty.description: the text of the test and of the reference are painted with instances of a variable font that should be the same: 56 antialiased pixels of the glyphs differ by 1 (the cause is not identified; the normalized coordinates of the two instances probably differ by a rounding error)

css/css-fonts/matching/font-unicode-PUA-.description: the `Arial` and `Times` fonts are not installed (the installed fonts are the bundled Tinos, Arimo and Cousine, without aliases): both pages render the Private Use Area characters with the missing glyph of the same default font (whose `.notdef` draws nothing)

css/css-fonts/matching/stretch-distance-.description: the text of the test and of the reference are painted with instances of a variable font that should be the same: 70 antialiased pixels of the glyphs differ by 1 (the cause is not identified; the normalized coordinates of the two instances probably differ by a rounding error)

css/css-fonts/matching/style-ranges-over.description: the text of the test and of the reference are painted with instances of a variable font that should be the same: 14 antialiased pixels of the glyphs differ by 1 (the cause is not identified; the normalized coordinates of the two instances probably differ by a rounding error)

css/css-fonts/variations/variable-avar2-.description: the fonts of the test (avar version 2) and of the reference (avar version 1) are not the same design: at `wght` 900 and `wdth` 75, the normalized `wght` coordinate is 8192 in the first one and 8193 in the second one (in 2.14 units, as HarfBuzz computes them), so the outlines of the third `H` differ by a fraction of a font unit and a few antialiased pixels of its edges differ; the test has no fuzzy tolerance

css/css-fonts/standard-font-family-11.ht.description: the quoted `'ui-serif'` is a family name, not the generic family (the generic families are unquoted keywords), and no installed font has this name: the text uses the default font, like the mismatch reference; only Safari, whose platform has fonts with these names, passes

css/css-fonts/standard-font-family-14.ht.description: `src: local("ui-serif")`: `local()` matches the full name or the PostScript name of an installed font, not a generic family, and no installed font has this name: the font face fails to load and the text uses the default font, like the mismatch reference; only Safari, whose platform has fonts with these names, passes

css/css-fonts/standard-font-family-15.ht.description: `src: local("ui-monospace")`: `local()` matches the full name or the PostScript name of an installed font, not a generic family, and no installed font has this name: the font face fails to load and the text uses the default font, like the mismatch reference; only Safari, whose platform has fonts with these names, passes

css/css-fonts/system-ui-ja-vs-zh.html.description: `system-ui` does not depend on the content language: the runner installs one fallback font per script (M+ 1p for the Han characters, Scheherazade for the Arabic letters), so the two pages, which only differ by their `lang` attribute, are painted with the same glyphs

css/css-fonts/system-ui-ur-vs-ar.html.description: `system-ui` does not depend on the content language: the runner installs one fallback font per script (M+ 1p for the Han characters, Scheherazade for the Arabic letters), so the two pages, which only differ by their `lang` attribute, are painted with the same glyphs; only Safari passes

css/css-fonts/font-display/font-display-.description: `font-display` (the block, swap and failure periods of the font display timeline): a font face is used whenever it is loaded, so the text of the `font-display: optional` face, whose font arrives after 1s (after its block period), is painted with the web font instead of the fallback font; Firefox fails too

`font-display` (the block, swap and failure periods of the font display timeline): the five texts are painted with the web font in the screenshot; 200ms after the start of the load of a font delayed by 5s, the text is expected to be invisible for `auto` and `block` (block period) and in the fallback font for `swap`, `fallback` and `optional`; only Firefox passes

css/css-fonts/font-display/font-display..description: `font-display` (the block, swap and failure periods of the font display timeline): each cell is painted with the web font when it is loaded and with the fallback font before, whatever the descriptor and the time elapsed (no invisible text during the block period, no end of the swap period); the test depends on the timings of the loads and fails in every browser

css/css-fonts/font-family-name-010.xht.description: the unquoted family name of the test contains U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE, which is not an ident code point (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax-3/#non-ascii-ident-code-point): the declaration is invalid and the text keeps the default font (the same name in a string, font-family-name-011.xht, selects the installed `CSSTest FamilyName` font by its localized name)

css/css-fonts/separators.html.description: U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR force a line break and are painted with their glyph (the `L` and `P` boxes of the test font): the test expects them to be rendered as a space, without line break (only Chrome passes)

css/css-fonts/font-variant-ligatures-11..description: the Arabic fallback font of the runner (Scheherazade) has no glyph for the Arabic presentation forms (U+FEDF and U+FE8E), which the reference uses to draw the lam and the alef without their ligature: the second line of the reference is empty, where the test paints the two letters without the `rlig` ligature as expected

css/css-forms/*.description: the references draw the controls with base appearance as Chrome does, not with the Basic Appearance User Agent Stylesheet of the specification that the library applies: the buttons, the color well and the text fields have `border-radius: 4px` in the specification (the references have 0.5em or none, so the corners differ); the track of a progress bar is a content box whose `inline-size: 100%` overflows the control by its borders; the fill of a meter is `currentColor` (the references color it by the state of the value, red, orange, green, with pseudo-classes such as `:even-less-good`); the tests fail in every browser of wpt.fyi but Chrome

css/css-gaps/flex/fragmentation/flex-gap.description: a row flex container with a specified block size whose two lines are separated by a forced break: the column rule between the items of a line runs across its line, which is stretched (80px), in each fragment; the reference (Blink) has rules of 30px, the block size of the items: at the start of the first fragment, and 50px after the start of the second one, whose items are at its start (the rule of Blink is not beside the items: not reproduced)

css/css-gaps/grid-lanes/column-gap-decor.description: `column-rule-visibility-items: between` and `row-rule-visibility-items: between` in a grid lanes container: the gap decoration segments are not limited to the parts of the gap between items when a lane ends before its neighbors

css/css-gaps/grid-lanes/row-gap-decorati.description: `column-rule-visibility-items: between` and `row-rule-visibility-items: between` in a grid lanes container: the gap decoration segments are not limited to the parts of the gap between items when a lane ends before its neighbors

css/css-gaps/grid/fragmentation/grid-gap.description: a grid with a block-start padding of 20px in columns of 10px: the padding is not broken, the row is in the second column in the test and in the reference, and the column rule of the test is between its two items; the reference (Blink) has the rule in the third column, at the offset of the row in the container before its fragmentation, without the items (not reproduced)

a grid with a block-start padding of 20px that starts 10px before the end of a column: the padding is in the second column in the test and in the reference, and the column rule of the test runs along the rows (from 20px to the end of the second column, then 80px in the third one); the rule of the reference (Blink) starts 10px before the first row and ends 10px before the end of the second one (the block size of the first fragment of the container is subtracted from the offsets of the rule but not from the ones of the items: not reproduced)

css/css-gaps/grid/subgrid/fragmentation/.description: a grid with a definite block size (140px, five rows of 1fr separated by gaps of 10px, columns of 80px) whose rows 2 to 4 are spanned by a subgrid and whose row 5 has an item: the gap between the rows 3 and 4, which the subgrid spans across, starts at the break and disappears; the library moves up the row right after it (row 4, which has no item), Blink moves up the first row of the next set of tracks (row 5: a set groups the adjacent tracks of one track definition, here repeat(5, 1fr), between the lines where items start or end), so the item of row 5 starts 10px earlier, over the visible gap before it (an artifact of the sets of Blink: with five separate track definitions, Blink would move row 4)

css/css-gaps/multicol/multicol-gap-decor.description: the column spanners in the rows of a fixed block size (`column-height`) of a nested multi-column container: the spanner and the rows after it are placed after the balanced content, where they are expected at the positions of the rows (the rows and their spanners are at fixed positions only in a container that is not nested)
