css/css-pseudo/first-letter-001.html.description: the white inline box of the no-break space covers its content area (56px for the 50px font), not the line box (58px with `line-height: normal`): 1px of the red background of the block is visible above and below it; fails in every browser

css/css-pseudo/first-line-font-relative-.description: the inline-axis border of an inline box on the first line (`border-left: 1em`) is laid out with the font size that the box has on the other lines (100px), not with the one it inherits from `::first-line` (10px): the text after it is 90px too far (the border is painted 10px wide)

css/css-pseudo/first-line-opacity-001.ht.description: the `opacity` of `::first-line` (the first line is not painted as a group); only Firefox passes

css/css-pseudo/highlight-painting-002.ht.description: the shadow of the selected text is painted under the text of the whole fragment, so the text after the selection is over the shadow that overlaps it, where the reference paints the selection overlay (its background, its shadow and its text) over the text that is not selected. `highlight-painting-shadows-*` expect the opposite order when two highlights apply (the text that is not highlighted over the shadows of the highlights): Blink, the only browser that passes both, has a painting path for a selection alone

css/css-pseudo/marker-content-008.tentat.description: 15 pixels differ by at most 18/255 on the edges of the glyphs: the text of the `::before` ("c") and the text of the list item are two text runs painted at fractional positions, where the reference paints one run ("cB")

css/css-pseudo/marker-letter-spacing.htm.description: the references expect the `letter-spacing` after the last character of an outside marker (as Chrome, the second reference) or only after its suffix (as Firefox, the first reference); the spacing "is not applied at the beginning or end of a line" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property): the outside markers, which are the only content of the line of their box, are 25px narrower

css/css-pseudo/marker-line-break.html.description: the test expects the text of a marker to wrap with `line-break: anywhere`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` or `word-break: break-all`, but the user agent style sheet of CSS Lists gives `white-space: pre` to `::marker` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#ua-stylesheet), which forbids the soft wraps; only Chrome passes

css/css-pseudo/marker-overflow-wrap.html.description: the test expects the text of a marker to wrap with `line-break: anywhere`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` or `word-break: break-all`, but the user agent style sheet of CSS Lists gives `white-space: pre` to `::marker` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#ua-stylesheet), which forbids the soft wraps; only Chrome passes

css/css-pseudo/marker-word-break.html.description: the test expects the text of a marker to wrap with `line-break: anywhere`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` or `word-break: break-all`, but the user agent style sheet of CSS Lists gives `white-space: pre` to `::marker` (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists-3/#ua-stylesheet), which forbids the soft wraps; only Chrome passes

css/css-pseudo/selection-background-pain.description: the part of the italic glyph after the selection that overhangs the selected text is not painted under the background of `::selection` (the reference paints the glyphs in two layers)

css/css-pseudo/selection-input-011.html.description: the selection of the value is highlighted with `::selection` as in the reference, but the reference focuses its `input` (it is painted with a focus ring): the test relies on `select()` giving the focus to the control, as in Chrome, which the standard does not specify (the only different pixels are the ones of the focus ring); Firefox and Safari fail too

css/css-pseudo/selection-over-highlight-.description: the background of `::selection` covers the content area of the text (ascent + descent), 1px shorter than the line box that the reference fills (the browsers extend the selection to the line box)

css/css-pseudo/selection-contenteditable.description: `Selection.addRange()` in a `contenteditable` element does not move the focus to the editing host, as the browsers do: the reference, which focuses the element, has a focus ring (`outline: auto`) that the test does not have

css/css-ruby/block-ruby-001.html.description: as in Gecko, no line break between the bases of a ruby segment without annotation (the reference uses `white-space: nowrap`): each base is a ruby column

css/css-ruby/block-ruby-002.html.description: the inlinification of the computed `display` of the block-level ruby containers in a ruby container (`block ruby` instead of `ruby`): the boxes are inlinified, not the computed values

css/css-ruby/block-ruby-005.html.description: the inlinified block-level ruby containers (`display: block ruby`) in an annotation or in a base container are not laid out as in the reference

css/css-ruby/break-within-bases/*.description: the line breaks inside the ruby bases (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#break-within): a ruby column is a unit of the line breaking (its items are the items of its bases followed by the items of its annotations), so breaking it needs the bases and the annotations to be broken at different positions on each line; Chrome only

css/css-ruby/collapse-trailing-whitespac.description: the reference pairs the base `n` with the annotation `n`, which is hidden (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#autohide: its text content is the text content of its base, as in Gecko), where the base `n ` of the test (with a space) keeps its annotation; the test passes in Chrome, which does not hide annotations (the trailing space of the base is removed at the end of the line as expected)

css/css-ruby/nested-ruby-pairing-001.htm.description: a ruby nested in a ruby base is 2px wider than the equivalent ruby with two annotation levels: the slots of the inner ruby columns are not widened by the annotation of the outer ruby

css/css-ruby/pseudo-first-line.html.description: the painting of the `color` of `::first-line`, and `ruby-position` in `::first-line`

css/css-ruby/rbc-rtc-basic-001.html.description: the column of an annotation without base (the second annotation of a ruby with one base) does not overhang the text after the ruby, where the column of the reference, whose base is a no-break space, overhangs the white space that follows it by 7.5px (`ruby-overhang: auto`): the next two rubies are 7.5px to the right (passes in Firefox only)

css/css-ruby/ruby-bidi-002.html.description: the order of the ruby segments and of the bases and annotations by the `direction` of their containers (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby-1/#bidi)

css/css-ruby/ruby-bidi-003.html.description: the annotation of mixed-direction text is expanded by `ruby-align: space-around` (its characters are spread) while the reference centers it; the Hebrew characters have no glyph in the fonts of the runner

css/css-ruby/ruby-box-generation-*.description: the reference assumes that the annotations do not overhang (`ruby-overhang: auto`: they "may overhang adjacent content"): the annotations wider than their base overhang the inter-segment white space before and after their column (`ruby-overhang: auto`, as Blink), where the reference (made for Gecko, which does not overhang) puts that white space in a ruby base of its own segment, which is not overhung: the columns `l` (002) and `t` (005) are 0.9px narrower than in the reference (passes in Firefox only)

css/css-ruby/ruby-inlinize-recursive-sim.description: the inlinified list item (`li`) in the ruby container and in the annotation is laid out 1px apart from the reference

css/css-ruby/ruby-intrinsic-isize-002.ht.description: the texts of the bases are shaped separately: no kerning between them, unlike the single text of the reference

css/css-ruby/ruby-intrinsic-isize-003.ht.description: a glyph of the bases next to the margins, borders and paddings of the ruby container is a fraction of a pixel off

css/css-ruby/ruby-justification-001.html.description: the expansion of the ruby columns by the justification of their line (`text-align: justify`): they are not expanded

css/css-ruby/ruby-overhang-spaces-013.ht.description: the test is made for a default font whose Latin `a` is half an ideograph wide (the Japanese fonts that the browsers use for `lang=ja`): with tab stops of `1ic`, the tabs before and after the ruby are then 0.5ic wide and the annotation overhangs them on both sides; the `a` of the default font of the runner is 0.44ic wide, so the tab after the column does not end on the tab stop that the reference assumes (and the overhang used by the line breaking, 11.1px, differs from the one of the positioned line, 20px: the box is 8.9px wider than its content); passes in Chrome only

css/css-ruby/ruby-overhang-spaces-019.ht.description: the test is made for a default font whose U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT is fullwidth (the Japanese fonts that the browsers use for `lang=ja`), with a blank quarter on each side that the annotation overhangs (5px); the middle dot of the default font of the runner is proportional (6.7px), and the annotation overhangs a quarter of it (1.7px): the test is 6.7px wider than the reference; passes in Chrome only

css/css-ruby/ruby-overhang-spaces-vertic.description: the Japanese fallback font of the runner (M+ 1p) has no vertical metrics (`vhea`, `vmtx`): its upright glyphs advance by the ascent and the descent of the font (1.395em) in vertical text, while the brackets that are set sideways advance by 1em; the reference assumes that the blank half of a bracket is half of the advance of an ideograph (the brackets set sideways are overhung by 10px, the reference expects 13.95px)

the Japanese fallback font of the runner (M+ 1p) has no vertical metrics (`vhea`, `vmtx`): its upright glyphs advance by the ascent and the descent of the font (1.395em) in vertical text, while the brackets that are set sideways advance by 1em; the reference assumes that the blank half of a bracket is half of the advance of an ideograph (the brackets set sideways are overhung by 10px, the reference expects 13.95px); the font has no `vhal` feature either

css/css-scroll-snap/scroll-target-align-.description: the optional use of the scroll snap alignment of the target (`scroll-snap-align: center`) by the scroll to the fragment when the scroll container has `scroll-snap-type: none` (test flagged `may`): the target is aligned at the start of the scrollport (with its `scroll-margin` and the `scroll-padding`), the green stripe is in the first quarter instead of the second one; only Firefox passes

the optional use of the scroll snap alignment of the target (`scroll-snap-align: center`) by `scrollIntoView()` when the scroll container has `scroll-snap-type: none` (test flagged `may`): the target is aligned at the start of the scrollport (with its `scroll-margin` and the `scroll-padding`), the green stripe is in the first quarter instead of the second one; only Firefox passes

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio/block-aspect.description: the percentage heights in a block with `aspect-ratio` resolve against the width of the previous layout when a shrink-to-fit ancestor measures it, so the block grows

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio/replaced-ele.description: the frames of the videos are not decoded: the media backend of the tests gives an opaque black frame, painted with `object-fit: contain` in the middle of the green box, where the test expects the green frame of the video

css/css-shapes/shape-outside/shape-image.description: the float area of the image with `shape-margin` is the expected one (the text is at 120px), but the test paints the 100x100 image, whose right half is transparent, scaled to 200x200 and compares it with a solid rectangle: the interpolation of the scaled image blurs the edge of its opaque half (400 pixels differ slightly); the test fails in all the browsers

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio/replaced-ele.description: the preferred `aspect-ratio` changes the size of the `audio` elements with `controls` (300x300 instead of 300x54 for the first one), which the test expects to keep the size of their controls, as in its reference without `aspect-ratio`

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio/grid-aspect-.description: the min-content contribution of a grid item that is a scroll container (`overflow: auto`) with `aspect-ratio: 2/1` and `height: 100px` is the size transferred through the ratio (200px) instead of 0 (it has no content and its automatic minimum size is 0): the `width: min-content` grid is 300px wide instead of 100px

css/css-sizing/aspect-ratio/select-eleme.description: the automatic minimum size (`min-width: auto`) of a `<select>` with `aspect-ratio: 1/1` and `height: 50px` is not its content size: it stays 50px wide instead of growing to the width of its selected option (171px); the rule is only applied to the non-replaced boxes

css/css-sizing/max-content-input-001.htm.description: expects `height: max-content` and `width: max-content` on `<input>` and `<textarea>` to be the size of their text (7 lines, 11ch, 27 columns) instead of their intrinsic size (`size`, `rows`, `cols`); fails in every browser

css/css-sizing/range-percent-intrinsic-s.description: the min-content size of a flex container whose `<input type=range>` item has `width: 50%; flex: 1` is the margins of the item (its cyclic percentage width zeroes its min-content contribution, as for the automatic minimum size of the compressible flex items) where the browsers keep the default width of the range: the container, a shrinkable flex item itself, is 71px wide instead of 135px (the other cases of the test, `min-width: min-content` with a percentage `width` or `max-width`, match)

css/css-tables/col-definite-max-size-001.description: the `<col>` elements without cell (4 columns for 2 cells): a column whose width is a percentage (`width: 50%`) or is limited by `max-width: 0` is kept with its `border-spacing` although its width is not definite (the table is 76px wide instead of 56px), and `min-width: 100px` is not applied to these columns (232px instead of 452px); only Firefox passes

css/css-tables/col-definite-min-size-001.description: the `min-width: 100px` of the `<col>` elements is not applied to the columns without cell (4 columns for 2 cells): they are 0px wide and the table is 232px wide instead of 452px; only Firefox passes

css/css-tables/col-definite-size-001.htm.description: a `<col>` without cell whose width is a percentage (`width: 50%`) is kept with its `border-spacing` (the table is 76px wide instead of 56px): as for `calc(100px + 1%)`, only the columns with a definite width should be kept; only Firefox passes

css/css-tables/tentative/paint/backgroun.description: 19 pixels on the boundaries of the pixels of the scaled background image of the column differ from the reference (the cause is not identified; probably the rounding of the samples that are exactly between two pixels of the image)

css/css-tables/visibility-collapse-colsp.description: the clipping of the contents of a cell that spans a collapsed column or row (`visibility: collapse`) to the shrunk box of the cell (css-tables-3 #visibility-collapse-cell-rendering): the overflowing text is painted; fails in every browser

css/css-tables/visibility-collapse-rowsp.description: the clipping of the contents of a cell that spans a collapsed column or row (`visibility: collapse`) to the shrunk box of the cell (css-tables-3 #visibility-collapse-cell-rendering): the overflowing text is painted; fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/invalidation/selectio.description: the `::selection` rule of the test draws black wavy lines (`text-decoration-color: black`) and the element of the reference green ones (`text-decoration-color: green`); fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-color.description: the last line expects the underline of a text with `-webkit-text-stroke-color: LinkText` to be painted in the color of the stroke; `text-decoration-color` is `currentcolor`, the black `color` of the text (only Safari passes)

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-inset.description: the reference draws the part of the underline that the inset adds after the text with trailing no-break spaces, which the initial `text-decoration-skip-spaces: start end` does not decorate (the test passes with `text-decoration-skip-spaces: none`; Firefox, which does not implement that property, passes; Chrome fails too)

css/css-text-decor/text-emphasis-punctua.description: the emphasis marks extend their line box by a fractional amount (1.5px above the half-leading of `line-height: 2`: the two lines of the test are 33.5px tall), where the two lines of the reference are 34px and 32px tall: the second line is 0.5px higher than in the reference and its text is antialiased at another position; fails in every browser

css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-decor.description: the transparent `x` lowered by `vertical-align: -10px` touches the underline of its decorating box (the top of its x-height is 0.3px inside the 1px line), and `text-decoration-skip-ink: auto` skips the underline across the glyph (8px); the `x` of the reference is on the baseline and its underline has no gap

css/css-text/bidi/bidi-lines-002.html.description: a bidi paragraph of `unicode-bidi: plaintext` without strong character takes the direction of its containing block instead of the direction of the previous paragraph (fails in every browser)

css/css-text/hanging-punctuation/hanging.description: the test is rendered as expected (the parentheses hang), but its reference emulates the hanging with an inline box that has negative margins and relies on the negative inline-end margin to bring back on the line the last word, which overflows it by 1em: as in Chrome and Firefox, the content of an inline box must fit on the line before its negative inline-end margin is applied (WPT css/css-grid/firefox-bug-1881495.html, which Safari fails), so the line of the reference is broken before the last word (Safari, the only browser with `hanging-punctuation`, is the only one that passes)

the reference fits 11 fullwidth characters on a line of 10em thanks to the trimming of the fullwidth punctuation (`text-spacing-trim: normal`: the opening bracket after the ideographic comma and the closing bracket at the end of the line are set half-width); the Japanese fallback font of the runner (M+ 1p) has no `halt` feature, so its punctuation is not trimmed (as in Chrome) and the line of the test breaks one character earlier; passes in Chrome only, with a system font that has the feature

css/css-text/hyphens/hyphens-auto-004.ht.description: the ideographic spaces (U+3000) after `regulation` hang at the end of its second line (CSS Text hangs the other space separators), the reference puts them on a line of their own, as Chrome and Safari do (Firefox fails too)

css/css-text/hyphens/hyphens-auto-contro.description: a monospace font with a U+2010 HYPHEN glyph like its U+002D: the bundled monospace font (Cousine) has no U+2010, the hyphen is the U+2010 of a fallback font (Tinos), the reference uses U+002D

css/css-text/hyphens/i18n/hyphens-i18n-a.description: the Dutch hyphenation patterns of hyph-utf8 have no hyphenation opportunity before the diminutive suffix of `cafeetje` (only `ca-feetje`), so its spelling change at the break (`café-tje`, implemented for the soft hyphens, `hyphens-i18n-manual-001`) is not used; no browser passes

there is no Hungarian hyphenation dictionary (the patterns of hyph-utf8 are under copyleft licenses), so `Összeg` is not hyphenated automatically (the spelling change `Ösz-szeg` is implemented for the soft hyphens, `hyphens-i18n-manual-002`); no browser passes
there is no Uyghur hyphenation dictionary (hyph-utf8 has none), so the word is not hyphenated automatically; no browser passes

css/css-text/hyphens/i18n/hyphens-i18n-m.description: the Uyghur word fits in the `4ch` of the box with the Arabic fallback font of the runner (Scheherazade, narrower than the fonts of the browsers), so it is not broken at the soft hyphen (where the hyphen would be U+0640 ARABIC TATWEEL); no browser passes

css/css-text/hyphens/i18n/hyphens-i18n-a.description: there is no Cree hyphenation dictionary (hyph-utf8 has none), so the syllabics are not hyphenated automatically (the hyphen after the Canadian syllabics is U+1400 CANADIAN SYLLABICS HYPHEN); the runner has no font for the Canadian syllabics; no browser passes

css/css-text/letter-spacing/letter-spaci.description: the test predates `text-autospace`: with its initial value `normal`, 1/8ic of inter-script spacing is added between a digit and an ideograph of `12三456七89` ("this property is additive with the word-spacing and letter-spacing properties"), so `12三` and `七89` are 5.125em wide and do not fit in the 5em box as the reference expects (the lines break next to the ideographs); the rest of the test matches, and the test with `text-autospace: no-autospace` is identical to its reference (fails in every browser)

the test expects a line to break between a U+200B and the preserved space after it (the space starts the next line, with its letter spacing); UAX #14 (LB7, LB8: `ZW SP* ÷`) only allows the break after the spaces that follow the U+200B, so the space hangs at the end of the line and the next line starts with the `x` (fails in every browser)

the reference is 2em wide (its two characters have no `letter-spacing`), the float of the test is 3em wide: two characters and the spacing of 1em between them (the spacing after the last character of a line is not applied, the invisible formatting characters that follow it being ignored), all green. Fails in every browser

css/css-text/line-breaking/line-breaking.description: the static position of an absolutely positioned `::before` at the start of an inline box that starts a new line is at the end of the previous line (the out-of-flow box is kept before the soft wrap opportunity), where the reference has it at the start of the new line (visible in the viewport since the monospace text is 13px; Chrome and Safari fail too)

css/css-text/letter-spacing/letter-spaci.description: the test expects the letter spacing model of the previous drafts of CSS Text 3: the spacing between two characters is the one of the innermost element that contains both of them (rendered inside that element, after the text-empty inline boxes between the characters). The current drafts (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property) add half of the spacing of each character on each of its sides, which gives other positions at the boundaries of the elements of this test, and note that the tests need to be updated; this engine adds the spacing of the element of a character after it, as the browsers (fails in every browser)

mathml/presentation-markup/mrow/legacy-m.description: the squares that the HTML parser moves out of `math` (the `span` child of `annotation` in the test, of `mrow` in the reference) and the ones it keeps in a token element are swapped between the test and the reference, and a line that contains an `mtext` or `annotation-xml` with the 50px inline-block is 56px tall (the strut of the bundled math font, STIX Two Math, has a 6px descent) while a line with the bare inline-block is 54px tall: the second square is 2px higher than in the reference; the test assumes a math font whose strut is not deeper than the one of the default font, only Chrome passes; the trees differ because of the HTML parser (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inforeign: a `span` start tag in foreign content pops the elements up to a MathML text integration point, an HTML integration point or an HTML element), and the height of a line depends on the strut of the font of its block container (CSS 2 section 10.8.1: "each line box starts with a zero-width inline box with the element's font and line height properties"; MathML Core user agent style sheet: `math { font-family: math; line-height: normal }`)

mathml/presentation-markup/operators/mo-.description: the rendering of the U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS content of an `mo` with the glyph of U+2212 MINUS SIGN (a WebKit behavior: the hyphen of the primary font is painted, 16.8px wide instead of 20.5px); only Safari passes

the test expects the spacing of the MathML 3 operator dictionary for U+223F SINE WAVE (lspace and rspace of 3/18em); this character is not in the operator dictionary of MathML Core, so it gets the default 5/18em (the `mo` is 1.8px further and the row 3.6px wider); Chrome fails too; MathML Core: the category of an operator that is not in the dictionary is Default, whose lspace and rspace are 0.2777777777777778em (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-algorithm-for-determining-the-properties-of-an-embellished-operator, https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#operator-dictionary); Firefox and Safari pass with the MathML 3 dictionary

mathml/presentation-markup/scripts/stret.description: the test expects the stretchy operator of the `mover` not to be stretched; with the algorithm for stretching operators along the block axis of MathML Core, the embellished operator is the only child of its row, so it is stretched to its own ink extent, which includes the overscript: the arrow is 50px tall instead of 25px; Chrome and Firefox fail too, only Safari passes; MathML Core (https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-algorithm-for-stretching-operators-along-the-block-axis): "If LNotToStretch is empty, perform layout with block stretch size constraint (0, 0) for all the items of LToStretch. the static-position rectangle of an absolutely positioned `display: block` box whose parent is an inline box is the one of the block layout (zero height at the start of the next line, as wide as the containing block) instead of the one of the inline layout (zero width at the inline-start edge, as tall as the 25px line): with `justify-self`/`align-self: end | center` the box is 100px/50px too far in the inline axis and 25px/12.5px too far back in the block axis; only Chrome passes

css/css-align/baseline-rules/synthesized.description: in the reference, the baseline of a baseline-aligned cell without line box is synthesized from the bottom of the content box of its specified `height` (150px, 230px) although its content (an empty `overflow: hidden` block of 50px, or of 80px with a 50px margin) is shorter: the browsers use the bottom edge of that content, as for the cell of the test whose content box is delimited by its paddings, so 2 of the 9 tables of the reference are 100px too high relative to the text; Safari fails

css/css-align/blocks/align-content-block.description: the contents of the broken box are not aligned (an accepted behavior), but the reference breaks before the float that does not fit in the second column (`break-inside: avoid`, in the middle of the inline content, after LINE 1) and leaves LINE 1 alone in that column, after the block with negative margins, where the library pushes the float to the next column and keeps the `orphans: 2` of the anonymous block, so LINE 1 starts the third column with the next lines

css/css-align/blocks/justify-self-widget.description: `justify-self: stretch` does not stretch the block-level form controls with `width: auto` (`<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`): they keep their intrinsic width (224px, 16px, 195px) instead of filling the 784px of the containing block; only Chrome passes

css/mediaqueries/at-custom-media-basic.h.description: the `@custom-media` rules are parsed (CSSOM) but the custom media queries are not evaluated: `@media (--foo)` is false; fails in every browser

css/mediaqueries/viewport-script-dynamic.description: `<meta name=viewport>` does not change the layout viewport (as in the desktop browsers: the test fails in every browser of wpt.fyi): the `(min-width: 310px)` query keeps matching the 800px viewport

css/css-values/calc-size/calc-size-aspec.description: the `min-width: calc-size(auto, size - 50px)` of a box with an `aspect-ratio` is not part of its intrinsic size contribution: its `width: fit-content` parent is 50px wide (the width transferred from the height) instead of 100px; only Chrome passes

css/css-values/calc-size/calc-size-flex-.description: the `height: calc-size(auto, min(size, 100px))` of a column flex container is resolved (100px) after its items were laid out in an indefinite main size, and the items are not flexed again in the definite size: they keep their 60px height and overflow instead of shrinking to 50px; only Chrome passes

css/css-values/viewport-units-scrollbars.description: the scrolling area of the reference is 4px larger than the one of the test in each axis (the borders of its content-box `div` are added to its size of 200%, where the test has them inside its border-box `body`): the thumbs of the scrollbars differ by 1px. The test fails in every browser (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

the non-standard `::-webkit-scrollbar` pseudo-elements: the test expects the viewport units to ignore the scrollbar of the root that they style (`100vw` is 800px, which overflows the scrollport as the 800px box of the reference does); the root has its classic scrollbar, whose gutter reduces `100vw` to 785px (`overflow-y: scroll`), and no horizontal scrollbar where the reference has one (the difference was not visible before the scrollbars were painted)

css/cssom/adoptedstylesheets-adopt-*.description: adopting the style sheet of a `style` or `link` element in `adoptedStyleSheets` (a tentative proposal: the specification only allows constructed style sheets and throws `NotAllowedError`); fails in every browser

css/css-grid/subgrid/independent-formatt.description: the test expects a fieldset with `display: grid` and `grid-template-rows: subgrid` to be a subgrid of its parent grid (Firefox and Safari); the grid container of a fieldset is its anonymous fieldset content box (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#anonymous-fieldset-content-box), whose parent, the principal box of the fieldset, is a block container that establishes a block formatting context: the content box is not a grid item, so `subgrid` behaves as `none` (as in Chrome, which fails this test too)

css/css-grid/grid-lanes/baseline/grid-la.description: expects the baseline content-alignment of the items in the stacking axis (`align-content: baseline | last baseline` on the items of a column grid lanes container, and on the vertical items of a row one): the reference is a grid whose items share the baseline of their contents in a row (a column), but "Baseline alignment is not supported in the stacking axis" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-3/#baseline-alignment; an earlier masonry draft aligned the items placed first in each track); the rows of `last baseline` items match. Fails in Chrome, Firefox and Safari

css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-016-pri.description: the monolithic content that does not fit in an empty page is sliced, but the box after a monolithic box that overflows into the next pages starts after the end of the monolithic box in the strip, and one more page is created, where Blink places it at the end of the sliced content (4 pages expected)

css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-017-pri.description: the monolithic content that does not fit in an empty page is sliced, but a float beside the monolithic content is not fragmented with it: it is placed in the first page and its part after the end of the page is clipped

css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-019-pri.description: the monolithic content that does not fit in an empty page is sliced, but a monolithic box in a parallel flow (a table cell) that overflows the page: the row is not broken in the strip, so its next pages are not created (2 pages instead of 4)

css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-023-pri.description: the monolithic content that does not fit in an empty page is sliced, but the content after a monolithic box that is sliced is placed in the page where the monolithic box ends, but not at its block-end edge (the second page differs)

css/css-page/monolithic-overflow-032-pri.description: the monolithic content that does not fit in an empty page is sliced, and a box with `box-decoration-break: clone` does not repeat its edges at the slices, but Blink also ends the fragment of the box right after the monolithic content (with its block-end edges) and starts a new fragment of the box after it in the same page (with its block-start edges): the content after the monolithic content is placed after the end of the monolithic content without these edges (the third and next pages differ)

css/css-page/body-background-srl-print.h.description: the canvas background of a `sideways-rl` root element stitched across two pages: the first page shows the right half of the gradient (lightgray), as the text of the test says, but the reference shows a white first page (Chrome and Firefox fail the test)

css/css-page/body-background-vrl-print.h.description: the background of the body stitched across the pages in `vertical-rl`: the fragments of the body are stitched in the block flow direction (the first page is the block-start, right, part of the stitched box), so the first page shows the white half of the gradient (`90deg`: lightgray on the left), where the reference expects the lightgray half on the first page (the absolutely positioned paragraph is placed as expected; no browser passes this test)

css/css-page/fixedpos-010-print.html.description: the fixed positioned box is placed as expected (laid out in the page area of the first page and repeated on the larger named pages), but the reference fails: its float (`float: right; margin-top: 300px`) overflows its container, which a forced page break (the change of page name) follows; the break is at the end of the container, so the float, after it in the strip, is placed in the next page instead of the page of its container (Blink breaks after the floats of the container)

css/css-page/fixedpos-011-print.html.description: a fixed positioned multi-column container repeated on every page: its columns are laid out as a nested multi-column container (the printing is the outer fragmentation context), and its clones on the next pages are not filled as in the first one

css/css-page/fixedpos-with-iframe-print..description: the nested documents of the `iframe` elements are painted as on the screen (not printed): the content of the frame is not the one of the print styles

css/css-page/layers-003-print.html.description: the layers of a stacking context split by the pages (`z-index`) are painted with the fragment of the stacking context of the same page; a few edge pixels of the text differ from the reference (subpixel positions of the text after the page area origin is snapped)

css/css-page/page-name-margin-001-print..description: the third page, whose page margin is 2cm (75.59px): the origin of its page area is snapped to the device pixels, which moves the content by 0.41px and rounds the block-end border of the box one pixel lower than in the reference, where the box is at the fractional position 2cm in an unsnapped page area (a few pixels of the edges differ)

css/css-page/page-name-zero-height-001-p.description: the boxes without block size that have a page name: each change of page name between them forces a page break (6 pages), where Blink does not start a page for a box without block size between two forced breaks (3 pages)

css/CSS2/pagination/float-page-break-ins.description: a float with `page-break-inside: avoid` that does not fit at the start of a block with a definite block size (the block crosses the end of the first page): the float is pushed, but the flow breaks before the block, which starts the second page with the float and the lines `X` and `Y` beside it, where the reference keeps the lines at the start of the block in the first page (laid out without the float) and only pushes the float to the second page

css/css-break/float-with-large-margin-bo.description: a float whose block-end margin (1in) does not fit in the rest of the first page: the float is pushed to the next page with its margin (the margin of a float is not truncated), where the reference keeps the float on the first page and continues its margin on the second one

css/css-break/table/repeated-section/fix.description: a fixed positioned box in a repeated table footer: the box is repeated on every page by the printing, and its repeated footers add other copies of it, which are placed at the static position of the footer of each fragment of the table

css/css-break/transform-024-print.html.description: absolutely positioned boxes with transforms in a rotated container (`rotate(180deg)`) split across five pages: the transform of each fragment of the container is applied with the transform origin of the fragment, not of the box stitched across the pages, so the red background of the container is visible

css/css-break/underflow-from-next-page-p.description: a box after a forced page break with a negative block-start margin (`margin-top: -50vh`): the box is placed before the break in the strip, so it ends on the first page and there is no second page, where Blink starts the second page with the box (the margin after a forced break is preserved and places it before the page area)

css/printing/emoji-print.html.description: an emoji font: the bundled fonts and the fonts of the runner have no glyph for the emoji, so the page is as blank as the mismatch reference

css/printing/existing-transition-in-medi.description: the transitions of the screen while printing (tentative): the print styles neither start nor update the transitions, so the running transition of the screen (to the color of `.print`) is not applied: the text keeps the red of the screen before the change, where the test expects the transition to be ended in the printed page

css/printing/page-overflow-crash-print.h.description: a quirks mode document whose `details` element has `offset-path` on all the elements: the motion path moves the content out of the page area, so the page is as blank as the mismatch reference

scroll-animations/css/printing/scroll-ti.description: the scroll-driven animations of the printing (tentative): the printed page uses the current values of the animations of the screen, where the test expects the scroll timeline to be inactive (the animation removed) in the printed page

css/css-grid/grid-lanes/intrinsic-sizing.description: `height: min-content`: the reference is the rendering of Chrome (the only browser that passes it; its comment says the reference may not be correct): the intrinsic inline size of the container (its stacking axis) is found with the items laid out in rows of infinite size, where the rows with a definite max track sizing function (`1.1ch`, `1.4ch`) keep their size and wrap the vertical items placed in them (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#algo-grid-sizing: "assume the available space that it would have if any row with a definite max track sizing function had that size and all other rows were infinite"), so the container is wider than the reference

`height: max-content`: the reference is the rendering of Chrome (the only browser that passes it; its comment says the reference may not be correct): the intrinsic inline size of the container (its stacking axis) is found with the items laid out in rows of infinite size, where the rows with a definite max track sizing function (`1.1ch`, `1.4ch`) keep their size and wrap the vertical items placed in them (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-2/#algo-grid-sizing: "assume the available space that it would have if any row with a definite max track sizing function had that size and all other rows were infinite"), so the container is wider than the reference

css/css-overflow/line-clamp/discard/disc.description: the test sets `block-ellipsis: auto`, the keyword of an earlier draft: `auto` is invalid in the current grammar `no-ellipsis | ellipsis | <string>` (WPT css/css-overflow/parsing/block-ellipsis-invalid.html), so the declaration is dropped and the last line before the region break has no ellipsis, where the reference has one (with `block-ellipsis: ellipsis` the rendering matches the reference)

css/css-overflow/scroll-markers/targeted.description: the scroll position after `scrollIntoView()` and the active scroll marker match the reference; the reference encodes the order of the scroll markers in the group of Blink, which lays out the `::scroll-marker` of the children before the `::column::scroll-marker` of their multi-column scroll container (while it increments the counters of the column markers first), where css-overflow-5 adds the markers "in the tree order of their originating element": the column markers of the container, then the markers of its children, so the labels and the positions of the markers differ

the scroll position after `scrollIntoView()` and the active scroll marker match the reference; the reference encodes the order of the scroll markers in the group of Blink, which lays out the `::scroll-marker` of the children before the `::column::scroll-marker` of their multi-column scroll container (while it increments the counters of the column markers first), where css-overflow-5 adds the markers "in the tree order of their originating element": the column markers of the container, then the markers of its children, so the labels and the positions of the markers differ

html/rendering/widgets/input-number-text.description: tentative (https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10390, only Firefox passes): the width of a number field does not depend on its `min`, `max` and `step` attributes (it is the width of a text field of 20 characters, as in Chrome); the test passed only while the text fields had no native frame (they were blank)
